depositSignature.selectorImpact: NONE. The 4-byte selector is computed from the argument types only, so deposit(address,uint256,address) is identical on both trees, and Solidity silently ignores surplus returndata when the caller's interface declares no return. PhusdStableMinter.sol:229 makes a bare statement call and will NOT brick against a master-tree strategy. This is a real ABI-drift class but it lands benign here.
depositSignature.semanticImpact: MATERIAL. On master, deposit returns creditedPrincipal, which stories 043/044/048/049 introduce precisely because a conservative ERC4626 crediting path can credit LESS principal than `amount`. PhusdStableMinter discards it (PhusdStableMinter.sol:229) and computes phUSD from `amount` (:212/:255), so the stable leg of an annihilation can be minted against principal that was not fully credited. Antimatter has zero visibility into this — its only post-condition on the deposit is the stablecoin-residue check at Antimatter.sol:230, which confirms the stable LEFT Antimatter, not that it was credited. Adjudicating the size and exploitability is interaction/econ-level; surfaced here as the trust assumption.
